Irene — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I reviewed their redlines and prepared a short annotated comparison (attached) with our recommended concessions. Quick notes:

- IP: We can accept a limited connector-specific carveout (their ask) provided we retain ownership of model outputs and pre-existing IP. I flagged a slightly stronger confidentiality tie to the connector language in the annotation.
- Data residency: Their suggested phrasing to permit processing in additional US regions is reasonable; add a logging requirement and a pin-option in the order form so customers can opt for a single-region deployment at additional cost.
- Order form qty/tiers: ops can confirm, but I think we can match their requested tier for Q3 with a small amendment to overage rates.

On signatures: I recommend we request a scanned signatory authority (signed corporate letter / POA) before sending the envelope. That lets us triage whether the listed signer has authority and avoids a failed envelope. We should prepare a DocuSign envelope with parallel recipients: Brightwell signer(s) + Redwood exec(s) in parallel, followed by automated distribution of the clean PDF to both parties and legal ops. If Brightwell insists on sequential flow, we can flip easily.

Attachment: Redlines_comparison_MSA_annotated.pdf

I'll defer to Marissa on whether we need additional language in the clean copy about delegated signing.

— Karthik
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
